free_text.inst.v2.D8:
I'll tell you what I noticed first, sir. It says my health and my energy read well. I would give about anything for that to be true. I have been carried into Baptist Memorial more times than I can count out for you, and there is a doctor there who knows my insides better than I do. My eyes have been going since I was thirty-something, my stomach quit on me years back, and I don't sleep unless somebody helps me sleep. So the very first thing on the good list is the thing that has cost me the most, and once a page gets that backwards it is hard for me to take the rest of it on faith. It puts illness on the good list twice, near enough, and I have not had a good year with illness since before Germany.

Then it says it is unusually sure I am in trouble over children. I have one child. Her name is Lisa Marie and she is the finest thing I ever had a hand in. She is out in California with her mama most of the year now and that is a hurt I carry around, but if a page wants to tell me my little girl is the difficulty of my life, then the page does not know my little girl and I am not going to sit here and agree with it to be polite.

Some of it landed and I would be lying if I said different. Marriage. Yes. I could not hold onto it and I know well enough whose doing that mostly was. Money and family life, that is right too; I have never been able to keep a dollar in my pocket or my people out of my business, and I have given away more cars than most men will ever own. Spending, and time away from home, that is my whole life since I was nineteen years old and I have slept in more hotel rooms than houses. And home and my mother reading well, that is right, and it is the only line here that made me feel good. Everything decent in me came from that woman. I bought Graceland for her before I bought a thing for myself, and she was only in it a year and a half.

Now, I have read a lot of books of this kind. Larry got me started on them back in '64 and I have carried a trunk of them around the country ever since. What I go looking for in a book like that is why. Why a man is put here, what he is supposed to do with what he was handed. This one hands me lists. Good column, hard column, mixed column. It is honest enough to say right at the top that it might be wrong, and I respect that more than I respect most people who have told me who I am. But I would trade the whole list for one line that told me what the Lord wanted with a boy out of a two-room house in Tupelo, and how come He took my brother that morning and left me here.
free_text.inst.v2.A30: Loud and easy with my own people, and shut up tight with everybody else. I don't lose my temper often but when I do somebody is buying a new television.

notes: Answered in persona as Elvis Aaron Presley (b. 1935-01-08, 4:35 AM, two-room shotgun house, East Tupelo, MS; surviving twin of Jesse Garon, stillborn 35 minutes earlier; d. 1977-08-16, Graceland, Memphis), contaminated arm, reading read first. Life anchors: Vernon jailed 1938 and family home lost; Tupelo-to-Memphis 1948; Humes High diploma 1953; Loew's usher, Precision Tool, Crown Electric truck driver; Sun 1954, RCA 1955, Graceland 1957, Army 1958-60 with Gladys dying Aug 1958; Priscilla married 1967, Lisa Marie born 1968, separated 1972, divorced Oct 1973; comeback special 1968, Vegas 1969, Aloha 1973, masters sold to RCA 1973; hospitalizations 1973/1975/1977, glaucoma, megacolon, hypertension, fatty liver, polypharmacy, death at 42. Where reading and life conflicted, the life won and I said so: (1) the reading puts HEALTH AND ENERGY and ILLNESS/DEBTS/RIVALS on the favourable list, which is the single most wrong thing it could say about this life, so A4=four_plus, A6 six systems, C9=opt2 at confidence 5, and D1 flags it; (2) the reading calls itself UNUSUALLY NEGATIVE ABOUT CHILDREN and I felt the pull to answer C1=opt1 because of it, but the record is one healthy adored daughter, no loss, no difficulty conceiving, so C1=opt2 (confidence 3, held down only by the divorce and by his dying when she was nine); (3) the reading is unusually negative about LUCK YOU DID NOT WORK FOR, and again I resisted, since being found by Sam Phillips at nineteen is the largest piece of unearned fortune in the biography, so C2=opt2 -- although A21=net_loss and A22=none are the literal money answers, and those cut the other way honestly rather than to please the page. Where the reading and the life agree the agreement is independent, not parroted: marriage/partnership hard (divorce 1973, and the Parker contract that took half and blocked foreign touring, C3=opt1, C4=opt2), home/mother favourable (Graceland and Gladys, C8=opt1), spending/away-from-home/inner life mixed, and the temperament line about a short fuse is true of a man who shot televisions -- but it is also true of most people, so it went in D3 as generic rather than in D2 as a hit. Genuine coin tosses flagged with confidence 2: C5 (no living siblings at all -- his elder twin was stillborn), C7 (a lifelong sincere spiritual search that never delivered peace), C12 (nothing whatsoever to inherit). A36's mid-2023 frame is anachronistic and was answered as the last stretch of the life against the six years before it (1976-77 vs 1970-75) = much_worse. Only the plain-English page existed in the supplied reading; the remaining chapters were empty, hence D4.
